lessonRef.subject: mathematics
lessonRef.title: Performance task planning: the ambiguous case

sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: This example shows how to justify a modelling choice.

sections.title: Guided practice
sections.directions: Decide what the quantities are before you compute anything.

items.prompt: In a triangle, angle A = 35°, angle B = 30°, and side a = 8 (opposite A). Find side b to two decimal places.
A triangle has sides a = 6 and b = 8 enclosing an angle of 30°. Find its area exactly.
A triangle problem gives all three sides (SSS). Which law should be used first?
choices: the law of sines, with a check for the ambiguous case

sections.title: Extension and challenge
sections.directions: Plan in writing: what you will model, why that model, and how you will check it.

items.prompt: In a triangle, sides a = 6 and b = 8 enclose an angle C = 60°. Find c², the square of the third side.
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.

items.prompt: In a triangle, angle A = 61°, angle B = 66°, and side a = 24 (opposite A). Find side b to two decimal places.
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.

items.prompt: A triangle has sides a = 16 and b = 4 enclosing an angle of 150°. Find its area exactly.
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.
